Team — quick ask to route for exec approval.

Summary: TinyClinics (YC-backed regional chain) wants to run a 6-week pilot on Dedicated. They will commit to a 3-month minimum term if we provide a one-time onboarding credit ~equal to $10k to reduce their Q3 cash impact. Prospect indicated procurement will sign quickly with an explicit credit callout.

Why this matters:
- Upside: If pilot shows value, conversion to a year-1 committed plan estimated at $180k ARR (conservative).
- Velocity: Procurement can sign within 48-72 hours if credit is authorized (sales velocity improvement).
- Low risk: Credit is one-time; we keep standard terms and retain the right to bill any overage.

Proposed structure (economics):
- Commitment: 3-month floor at pilot rates (monthly minimum $8k)
- One-time onboarding credit: $10,000 applied against first invoice
- Condition: Technical kickoff by 2026-09-07 and SOW executed before kickoff

Trade-offs/comp considerations:
- If TinyClinics converts to a 12-month contract within 90 days, propose to reverse 50% of the credit as an uplift (i.e., $5k reclamation via amendment).
- If they fail to hit usage minimums, credit is non-refundable (accounting write-off).

Attachments: pricing spreadsheet (20260823-pricing-summary.xlsx) and draft terms (redwood-terms-draft.pdf).

Requested approvals:
- Marcus Lin (Finance): confirm write-off accounting treatment and whether $10k fits the delegated approval threshold.
- Marissa Cole (Sales Leader): endorsement for velocity-based exception.
- Lauren Bishop (VP/Finance): final sign-off for any credit > $7,500.
